article_title: Research on the student-centered research feedback experimental teaching model to enhance the effectiveness of pharmacology experimental teaching.
citation: Miao C, Chen J, Li Y, Xia A, Song Y, Xu C, Mao Y, Wang X. (2026). Research on the student-centered research feedback experimental teaching model to enhance the effectiveness of pharmacology experimental teaching. Medicine. https://doi.org/10.1097/MD.0000000000051199
title: Quantitative evaluation of learning process (QELP) instrument for pharmacology experimental courses
description: QELP is a multi-component evaluation developed by the college's Experimental (Training) Teaching Center, "divided into 4 aspects: online scores, midterm scores, experimental report scores, final scores, and composite scores (the average score of the above 4 items)." Each evaluation is scored to a maximum of 100 points, with final scores covering 10 teaching projects averaged across key experimental-operation scoring points rated by the guiding teacher during class. The article uses QELP to compare TPETM and RFPETM groups across the learning process.
requirements: Key experimental operations defined as scoring points for each teaching project
constraints: Developed by a single institution's teaching center; final-score distribution used five fixed evaluation levels
